title.en: Properties of metals and the reactivity series

text.en: A copper wire bends and conducts electricity while sulphur crumbles. What makes metals different from non-metals, and which metals are the most reactive?

Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity. They are generally hard with high melting points.
Exceptions: sodium and potassium are soft, mercury is a liquid, and gallium has a very low melting point. Non-metals like diamond and graphite behave differently.
Non-metals are brittle, not malleable or ductile and usually poor conductors. Graphite conducts and diamond has the highest melting point.
Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides. Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric because they react with both acids and bases.
Reaction with water: sodium and potassium react violently, calcium reacts less vigorously, magnesium reacts only with hot water and iron with steam.
With dilute acids most metals release hydrogen. Copper, silver and gold do not.
The reactivity series arranges metals in order of decreasing reactivity: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution.

problem.en: Will zinc displace iron from iron sulphate solution?

text.en: Zinc is above iron in the reactivity series.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one.

prompt.en: What are the key properties and reactivity order of metals?
